## Owner's conditions (DEC-401)
- **Criss-cross: PASS.** With two or three merge bases, no base, or an octopus where one parent crosses (either order), nothing counts as brought and the merge is flagged.
- **Replay: PASS.** 174 real merges were read (171 on `w1/integrate`, 3 on this branch); none is flagged by mistake.
  - 22 merges have a non-empty own change; all are true hand resolutions from 18–26 September, none under `tests/acceptance/**`, all silent.
  - On the 44 merges since 1 October, the replaced DP-15 rule would have given 21 false findings; the new rule gives 0.
  - Limits: only merge commits were judged, and the freeze placeholder was patched out inside the reviewer's own process.
- **How the replay ran:** in place, read-only, on this worktree's objects. I did not let the reviewer make a temporary clone, because the standing rule forbids any worker cloning this repository (the held-out file would come with it).

## Reviewer findings (commit `796a69cc`)

| Finding | Severity | What was done |
|---|---|---|
| F1: a merge commit that keeps its first parent's content and drops what another parent changed is never judged | lets acceptance tests be changed; there before this commit | Needs a decision: DP-20 below. Not fixed. |
| F2: with F1, a second merge on top gets the wrong path named | minor | Goes away with F1's fix. |
| F3: `read_merge` raises the private `_GitError`; an option-like `commit` such as `--all` is read as an option; `own=[]` means only "same tree as first parent" | minor; introduced this round | Not fixed. Needs no decision; best folded into the engineer turn after DP-20, since W1-11 imports the helper. |
| F4: a merge commit in a worker's call is one "not a forward move" finding with no paths named | minor; there before (DEC-266) | Residual. |

- **F1 in detail.** `read_merge` looks only at what differs from the first parent. The reviewer ran seven shapes through the real hooks in an orchestrator's own call; all are silent:
  - parents turned round, with or without an extra empty commit;
  - plain `git merge -s ours main` on a temporary branch, then a fast-forward of `main`;
  - an octopus turned round;
  - a no-base merge turned round;
  - **shape N:** a ticket branch takes `main` with `git merge -s ours`, then an ordinary `--no-ff` merge of that branch into `main`. The final merge looks ordinary, and the undone tests are read as brought by the branch.
- The same root cause would undo a `.tickets/**` narrowing or close made on `main`; that one is reasoned, not run.
- **Cost of the rule:** 5 git processes per two-parent merge, about 7 ms each merge on the real repository. A move of 50 merges takes about 0.3 s; the largest real move (125 commits, 22 merges) 317 ms. A call without a HEAD move, and a move without merges, pay nothing new.
- **DP-17:** no evasion found (rename, symlink, path spelling, subagent all flagged) and no new noise.
- False findings by the reviewer: none.

## Package DP-20 — a merge that drops another parent's change (F1)
- **Question:** should a path where the merge commit differs from any parent, not only the first, count as the merge commit's own change unless another parent brought it by the three-way rule?
- **Why now:** this is a fail-open on `tests/acceptance/**` in the orchestrator's own call. DEC-394 and DEC-398 say "against its first parent", and DEC-398 fixes the helper's contract that W1-11 will import. A fix is wider than both.
- **Options:**
  - (a) Symmetric rule in the helper: read every parent the way the first is read. `own` then also holds paths where the merge drops a non-first parent's change, so own ∪ brought is no longer "exactly the first-parent diff". With several bases or no base, every path differing from any parent is own.
  - (b) Keep the helper as it is and add the drop check in containment only. The approval check would then read merges differently, against DEC-398's "one helper".
  - (c) Leave it and record a residual.
- **Impact:**
  - (a) closes all seven shapes. The reviewer's trial of it flagged the turned-round merge and shape N, and gave the same answers as today on eight of the suite's shapes and on all 174 real merges.
  - Under (a), a fail-closed criss-cross merge also lists the first-parent side's own work as the merge's own change. That is more noise, but only on rare histories.
  - (c) leaves a plain-porcelain way to undo acceptance tests silently.
- **Reversibility:** high; one helper, before W1-11 uses it.
- **Cost:** one design batch, one engineer turn (about 15–25 lines), one review; about 3 more git processes per merge commit.
- **Recommendation:** (a), with F3's two small fixes (a public error name, refuse a non-id `commit`) in the same engineer turn.
- **Confidence:** medium-high.

## Package DP-19 — octopus merge with one crossing parent (designer; built stricter)
- **Question:** when only one of an octopus merge's other parents has several merge bases, or none, with the first parent, does the whole merge fail closed, or only that parent?
- **Why now:** DEC-398's fail-closed wording describes a two-parent merge; the helper must answer for three or more, and W1-11 will use it.
- **Options:** (a) the whole merge fails closed; (b) only that parent brings nothing.
- **Impact:** (a) reports more — a clean branch's test-designer paths in such an octopus become the merge's own change. The real history has no octopus merge.
- **Reversibility:** high. **Cost:** nothing for (a); two or three cases to pin whichever is chosen.
- **As built:** (a). I told the engineer to build it as the stricter reading; no acceptance test pins either answer yet.
- **Recommendation:** confirm (a). **Confidence:** medium.
- **Related note for the same answer:** an octopus whose two other parents cross each other, each with one base against the first parent, counts paths as brought. That matches the decision's words, and the reviewer found no harm.
